title: Yoisaki Kanade — Early Morning Struggles〔Part2〕Side Story (Part 2)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (I started working on a new song in order to turn what I felt when I saw Ena's dad's art into music...)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (But I'm having so much trouble capturing it in sound...)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: What was that painting named again...? “A Peony Blooming in the Night”...?

rows.Speaker: Mizuki
rows.Line:
Alright, we're pretty far in now.
The next painting is...

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (This painting resonates with me so much more than the other ones for some reason. But why...?)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (His other paintings all involved darkness in some way, and they seemed to be an expression of his pain and suffering. But this one...)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (I want to try putting this sensation into a song...)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (I even bought a book of his paintings to make sure that I don't forget what I felt that time...)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (But that painting still stands above the rest for me.)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (I don't know what Ena's dad felt when he made that painting...)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (I want to turn what I felt into a song.)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line:
*Nod*
(I feel like it captures what I felt that time.)

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: <It's already morning. Did you stay up all night working...?>

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line:
<Huh? Oh, you're right.
I didn't realize that it was morning already.>

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: <Geez... Promise me that you'll at least take a nap later, okay? At the same time, I'm one to talk...>

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: <Yeah. After I logged off yesterday, I noticed something about my illustration that I didn't like. I was fixing that until now.>

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: <Anyway, I was about the send my file over, and I saw that you were online. That really took me by surprise.>

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (Wait, only Ena and I are here right now. This could be my chance to...)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: <So, there's a song that I'd like for you to listen to...>

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: <Wait, you already composed another song...?! You work way too fast!>

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line:
<Oh, but it's not for N25.
It's something that I just felt like composing is all...>

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: <So, would you mind listening to it?>

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: <Okay. I do want to hear what it's like, so I'll give it a listen...>

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: <Thank you. I'll send it over now.>

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: <For starters, it felt a little different from the songs you usually compose...>

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line:
<A little different...?
Can you elaborate on that?>

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: <Hmm... The songs you compose for N25 usually involve seeing the light at the end of a long, dark tunnel so to speak. But with this song...>

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line:
<The light took center stage...
It felt like something incredibly precious that you couldn't go on without. Like it meant everything.>

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: <Something that I can't go on without...?>

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: <Also, why did you want me to listen to it?>

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line:
<Oh, so...
I based this song on what I felt when I saw one of your dad's paintings.>

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: <It was the painting called “A Peony Blooming in the Night”... Something about it felt special.>

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: <I didn't realize that painting would turn into this kind of song...>

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (That exhibit was definitely worth the trip.)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (Not only did I get to see all those paintings, but I was also able to compose a kind of song that I usually don't...)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (I still don't know what Ena's dad was feeling when he painted that peony...)

rows.Speaker: Kanade
rows.Line: (But I hope that my song was able to do it some justice.)
